bib.title: Agentopia: Long-Term Life Simulation and Learning in Agent Societies

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Agentopia: Long-Term Life Simulation and Learning in Agent Societies", Xintao Wang, Sirui Zheng, Hongqiu Wu, Weiyuan Li, Jen-tse Huang et al. (Fudan, JHU, USTC, independent), arXiv 2606.07513v1 [cs.CL], 5 Jun 2026, preprint.

COVERAGE: 224,280 chars extracted. I read all of the main body (abstract through Limitations, about the first 60k chars) closely. I read the appendix selectively: B.1, B.17, C.1, D.1, D.11 and D.12 in full, plus a keyword search of the whole text. I did NOT read the rest of the appendix line by line: world/character creation (A), prompt tables, per-world tables, D.2-D.10, and the case studies in E (about 60 behavioral cases). That is a partial read of the appendices, not a complete read. I found nothing in the keyword search relevant to your target topic.

FIT WARNING: POOR for 04b-when-more-agents-pay. Agentopia is a social-simulation and LLM-fine-tuning paper. It never compares multi-agent with single-agent systems, never matches compute, and never measures a task where agent count could pay. The nearest content is a cost profile (below). Do not cite it for equal-compute multi-agent claims. At most it is a "scale and cost of agent societies" footnote. The keyword search found no "single-agent", "ablation" or "compute-matched" content.

CLAIMS (ranked by usefulness)
1. Life-reward SFT raises absolute social recognition but trades off other metrics.
   number: respected-by +24.2%, liked-by +15.9%, mutual respect +15.3%, mutual like +5.9%; economy +2.5%, subjective +1.8%; material fulfillment -14.8%, solo activity -19.8%, skill advances -29.6%
   setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B SFT on the top-25% advantage trajectories from years 1-4 of all 3 worlds. Evaluated in 4-year simulations on The Campus and The Apartment only, cross-world average, against the untuned model in identical worlds. One epoch, 30 nodes of 8xH100. No seeds or variance reported.
   quote: "Respected By 7.1 6.9 9.4 11.0 10.4 14.1 11.2 15.2 9.5 11.8↑24.2%" and "Mutual Like 4.1 3.9 5.2 5.3 5.5 6.4 5.6 6.0 5.1 5.4↑5.9%" and "Skill Advances 11.9 11.3 11.3 9.2 14.7 8.2 15.1 8.6 13.3 9.3↓−29.6%"
   where: Table 2, p.14
2. Training generalizes to role-play.
   number: +15.6% overall on CoSER Test; Anthropomorphism +23.7%, Character Fidelity +16.4%
   setup: judged by Qwen3-235B. Average 49.16 vs 42.51 for the base model, and above Claude 4.5-Sonnet at 45.21.
   quote: "yielding a 15.6% overall improvement on CoSER Test, with the largest increases in anthropomorphism (+23.7%) and character fidelity (+16.4%)."
   where: Conclusion, p.16; Table 3, p.15
3. The gain appears only over time.
   number: by Year 4, +35.7% respected, +22.2% liked, +21.7% mutual-respect ties
   setup: same 4-year runs, two worlds
   quote: "by Year 4, agents driven by Qwen3.5-397B-Agentopia are respected by 35.7% more peers, liked by 22.2% more, and hold 21.7% more mutual-respect ties"
   where: App. D.1, p.40
4. Cost of a 10-year, 100-agent world.
   number: 13.7B tokens, 567K calls, about 186 h on average. Per-week runtime rises from about 80 to 140 min.
   setup: 3 FP8 instances of Qwen3.5-397B per run. Input tokens dominate: 13,347M input vs 352M output.
   quote: "a single 10-year simulation consumes 13.7 billion tokens across 567K LLM calls, completing in approximately 186 wall-clock hours."
   where: Sec. 5.4, p.16; Table 4, p.15
5. Memory growth is the named bottleneck.
   number: none
   quote: "This indicates that memory growth serves as a major computational bottleneck for long-horizon social simulation"
   where: p.16
6. Role-playing agents account for most of the input tokens, and joint activities dominate the environment model's.
   number: RP agents about 95% of input tokens; joint activity over 70% of environment-model input tokens
   quote: "Role-playing agents account for approximately 95% of all input tokens" and "accounting for over 70% of environment model input tokens"
   where: App. D.12, p.52
7. Model comparison shows no dominant backbone.
   number: Gemini-3-Flash total +0.10, GPT-5-mini +0.06, Qwen3.5-397B -0.03 (z-scores)
   setup: 5 models, 20 agents each per world, 4 years, 2 worlds. These are z-scores and the paper does not report any significance test.
   quote: "A notable social–economic trade-off emerges: models that excel in economic metrics (GPT-5-mini) tend to underperform in social metrics"
   where: App. D.11, p.52
8. Design claim: abstract weekly social turns keep cost manageable.
   number: none
   quote: "This abstraction enables the system to model richer social behaviors with fewer LLM calls"
   where: Sec. 3.2, p.6. This is asserted, not measured against an alternative.

BASELINES: There is no single-agent baseline. The only comparison is the same multi-agent society run with the base model versus the tuned model, so the variable is the backbone model, not agent count or topology. Compute is not matched: the tuned model is fine-tuned on 30x8 H100s. The advantage baseline is "each agent's own previous return", because the paper says each agent has only one life trajectory. Each condition has a single run, with no seeds or confidence intervals.

LIMITS (authors): turn-based design; hallucination not eliminated; the environment and numeric systems do not match reality; the reward may not align with human well-being; all feedback comes from AI models, not humans. They also concede: "we did not conduct simulations with more worlds, more agents, or longer time horizons, nor trained on different model families", and no credit assignment finer than whole agent-year trajectories. My reading: training data comes from years 1-4 but the model is evaluated only on years 1-4 of two worlds, and the judge for CoSER is a Qwen model, the same family as the tuned model.

BUILDS ON: Generative Agents (Park et al., 2023); Project Sid (AL et al., 2024); Aivilization (Fan et al., 2026); Humanoid Agents (Wang et al., 2023); CAMEL (Li et al., 2023); CoSER (Wang et al., 2025); Maslow (1943); PageRank (Page et al., 1999); Warmth-Competence model (Fiske et al., 2007); PPO and GRPO (as the infeasible alternatives); Tulu 3 self-distillation mix (Lambert et al., 2024; Lu and Lab, 2025).

CODE: none in the paper (repo: https://github.com/Neph0s/Agentopia). Snippets worth keeping (formulas): advantage A_{i,t} = G^norm_{i,t} - G^norm_{i,t-1} (Sec. 4.2, p.11); select the top 25% of agents by advantage per period; 50:50 mix with Tulu 3 self-distilled data, by output tokens.

FIGURE candidate: Figure 2, p.3, "Overview of Agentopia". It shows the weekly Plan/Contact/Activity/Review loop, the year-end update, and the rejection-sampling training loop. It is useful for 05-topology-patterns, not for 04b.

PROBLEMS: Text extraction is clean, apart from some run-together words. No embedded instructions found. The tables in the extraction are flattened, so column alignment in the Table 2 quotes is inferred from the header.

AUDIT of ai-engineering/05-graph-engineering/notes/05-topology-patterns.md line 335 (references.md line 47 is fine; arXiv URL at line 20 is fine).
The note says: "Agentopia runs 100 agents for ten simulated years on a weekly Plan → Contact → Activity → Review loop, and fine-tuning on the top 25% of trajectories improved social metrics by 15–24%."
- Correct: 100 agents, 10 simulated years, the weekly loop with those four stages, and top 25% by advantage.
- Needs correction (1): the "100 agents × 10 years" is per world, and there are three worlds. Say "three worlds of 100 agents each".
- Needs correction (2): "15-24%" is selective. Three social-evaluation metrics rose 15.3-24.2%, but mutual like rose only 5.9%. Economy rose only 2.5% and subjective reward 1.8%. Material fulfillment fell 14.8%, solo activity fell 19.8% and skill advances fell 29.6%. It also omits the setup: the model is Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, trained on years 1-4, evaluated on 4-year runs in two of the three worlds, with no seeds or variance reported. "Top 25% of agents by advantage" is also more exact than "trajectories". It is SFT on each selected agent's whole yearly trajectory.
- Suggested replacement: "...and SFT of Qwen3.5-397B on the top 25% of agents by year-over-year return gain raised peer-respect by 24.2%, liked-by by 15.9% and mutual respect by 15.3% in four-year runs on two worlds (single run), but mutual like by only 5.9%, economy by 2.5%, material fulfillment fell 14.8% and skill advances fell 29.6% as agents learned to save and do fewer solo activities."
- Scope: nothing in the note claims multi-agent beats single-agent, so there is no false claim there. The note's framing as "no task at all, only agents living together" matches the paper.
